19478-four-day-planet.title: Four Day Planet
19478-four-day-planet.creator: Unknown
19478-four-day-planet.description: A public-domain book from Project Gutenberg. , because they weren't arguing about whose ship was fastest, had the toughest skipper, and made the most money. They were talking about the price of tallow-wax, and they seemed to have picked up a rumor that it was going to be cut another ten centisols a pound. I eavesdropped shamelessly, but it was the same rumor I'd picked up, myself, a little earlier.

arxiv-2209-05398.title: High-temperature kinetic magnetism in triangular lattices
arxiv-2209-05398.creator: Ivan Morera, Márton Kanász-Nagy, Tomasz Smolenski, Livio Ciorciaro, Ataç Imamoğlu, Eugene Demler
arxiv-2209-05398.description: Abstract We study kinetic magnetism for the Fermi-Hubbard models in triangular type lattices, including a zigzag ladder, four- and six-legged triangular cylinders, and a full two- dimensional triangular lattice. We focus on the regime of strong interactions, U ≫ t U\gg t and filling factors around one electron per site.

arxiv-2409-14299.title: Non-reciprocal frequency conversion in a multimode nonlinear system
arxiv-2409-14299.creator: Sahil Pontula 1,2,3, Sachin Vaidya 1, Charles Roques-Carmes 3,4, Shiekh Zia Uddin 1,3, Marin Soljačić 1,3, Yannick Salamin 1,3,5
arxiv-2409-14299.description: Abstract Nonlinear optics has become the workhorse for countless applications in classical and quantum optics, from optical bistability to single photon pair generation. However, the intrinsic weakness of optical nonlinearity has meant that large input powers and weak output powers are often a necessity in nonlinear frequency conversion.

arxiv-2501-12142.title: Anti-integrable limits for generalized Frenkel-Kontorova models on almost-periodic media
arxiv-2501-12142.creator: Jianxing Du, Xifeng Su
arxiv-2501-12142.description: Abstract . We study the equilibrium configurations for generalized Frenkel-Kontorova models subjected to almost-periodic media. By contrast with the spirit of the KAM theory, our approach consists in establishing the other perturbation theory for fully chaotic systems far away from the integrable, which is called “anti-integrable” limits.

arxiv-2505-16959.title: Bigger Isn’t Always Memorizing: Early Stopping Overparameterized Diffusion Models
arxiv-2505-16959.creator: Alessandro Favero, Antonio Sclocchi, Matthieu Wyart
arxiv-2505-16959.description: Abstract Diffusion probabilistic models have become a cornerstone of modern generative AI, yet the mechanisms underlying their generalization remain poorly understood. In fact, if these models were perfectly minimizing their training loss, they would just generate data belonging to their training set, i.e., memorize, as empirically found in the overparameterized regime.

arxiv-2506-19218.title: Stratified Hyperbolicity of the moduli stack of stable minimal models, II: Big Picard Theorem and the stratified Brody hyperbolicity
arxiv-2506-19218.creator: Junchao Shentu
arxiv-2506-19218.description: Abstract . This is the second paper on the global geometry of Birkar’s moduli of stable minimal models (e.g., the KSBA moduli stack). We introduces a birationally admissible stratification of the Deligne-Mumford stack of stable minimal models, such that the universal family over each stratum admits a simple normal crossing log birational model.

arxiv-2508-16253.title: Fault-tolerant quantum computations of vibrational wave functions
arxiv-2508-16253.creator: Marco Majland, Rasmus Berg Jensen, Patrick Ettenhuber, Irfansha Shaik, Nikolaj Thomas Zinner, Ove Christiansen
arxiv-2508-16253.description: Abstract Quantum computation of vibrational properties of molecules is a promising platform to obtain computational advantages for computational chemistry. However, fault-tolerant quantum computations of vibrational properties remain a relatively unexplored field in quantum computing. In this work, we present different algorithms for efficient encodings of vibrational Hamiltonians using qubitization.

arxiv-2509-07052.title: Exact solution of the DeWitt-Brehme-Hobbs equation in copropagating electromagetic and gravitational waves
arxiv-2509-07052.creator: Giulio Audagnotto, Antonino Di Piazza
arxiv-2509-07052.description: Abstract An accelerated charge interacts with itself through the electromagnetic field that it sources, a phenomenon known as electromagnetic radiation reaction. The DeWitt-Brehme-Hobbs (DWBH) equation describes the motion of a charged mass in the presence of combined electromagnetic and gravitational fields, taking into account electromagnetic radiation-reaction effects.

arxiv-2602-10863.title: ICA: Information-Aware Credit Assignment for Visually Grounded Long-Horizon Information-Seeking Agents
arxiv-2602-10863.creator: Cong Pang, Xuyu Feng, Yujie Yi, Zixuan Chen, Jiawei Hong, Tiankuo Yao, Nang Yuan, Jiapeng Luo, Lewei Lu, Xin Lou
arxiv-2602-10863.description: Abstract Despite the strong performance achieved by reinforcement learning–trained information-seeking agents, learning in open-ended web environments remains severely constrained by low signal-to-noise feedback. Text-based parsers often discard layout semantics and introduce unstructured noise, while long-horizon training typically relies on sparse outcome rewards that obscure which retrieval actions actually matter.

pmc-11352322.title: MiRNAs as Regulators of Immune Cells in the Tumor Microenvironment of Ovarian Cancer
pmc-11352322.creator: Miłosz Wilczyński, Jacek Wilczyński, Marek Nowak, Yves St-Pierre
pmc-11352322.description: Ovarian cancer is one of the leading causes of cancer deaths among women. There is an ongoing need to develop new biomarkers and targeted therapies to improve patient outcomes. One of the most critical research areas in ovarian cancer is identifying tumor microenvironment (TME) functions. TME consists of tumor-infiltrating immune cells, matrix, endothelial cells, pericytes, fibroblasts, and other stromal cells.

pmc-11361463.title: A Case of Basal Ganglia Intraparenchymal Hemorrhage Following Lumbar Spinal Surgery
pmc-11361463.creator: Michael J Gigliotti, Neel Patel, Chanju Fritch, Ephraim W Church, George T Reiter, Hajoe Park
pmc-11361463.description: We report on a rare case of basal ganglia intraparenchymal hemorrhage with intraventricular extension occurring after a lumbar spinal surgery. A 65-year-old female presented for an elective L4-L5 lumbar laminectomy and posterior spinal fixation. Her initial operation was complicated by a cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) leak repaired with a dural synthetic graft.

pmc-11441613.title: ‘A tool for every job’: use of video in urgent primary care
pmc-11441613.creator: Ulrik Bak Kirk, Rebecca Payne, Jaime-ann Tweedie, Linda Huibers
pmc-11441613.description: ut much of the research focuses on secondary care settings and specific sub-populations, such as those with diabetes.2 Despite studies from Denmark,3 Norway,4 Sweden,5 and the UK,6 a lack of evidence remains regarding the use of video in primary care, particularly outside office hours for patients seeking urgent care.

pmc-11476783.title: Flexible multimaterial fibers in modern biomedical applications
pmc-11476783.creator: Jongwoon Kim, Xiaoting Jia
pmc-11476783.description: Biomedical devices are indispensable in modern healthcare, significantly enhancing patients’ quality of life. Recently, there has been a drastic increase in innovations for the fabrication of biomedical devices. Amongst these fabrication methods, the thermal drawing process has emerged as a versatile and scalable process for the development of advanced biomedical devices.

pmc-11600649.title: Factors associated with quality of postnatal care in Kenya: an analysis of the 2022 Kenya demographic and health survey
pmc-11600649.creator: Lilian Nuwabaine, Angella Namulema, Quraish Sserwanja, Joseph Kawuki, Earnest Amwiine, Mathius Amperiize, Mary Grace Nakate, John Baptist Asiimwe
pmc-11600649.description: IntroductionDespite the significant contribution of postnatal care (PNC) to maternal and newborn survival, few studies have explored the concept of the quality of PNC received by mothers in Kenya. Therefore, this study aimed to determine the prevalence and factors associated with the quality of PNC in Kenya.

pmc-11712199.title: An Interprofessional Team for Disease Modifying Therapy in Alzheimer’s Disease Implementation
pmc-11712199.creator: Katherine W Turk, Mark D Knobel, Alexandra Nothern, Garrett Friedman, Hannah Noah, Brendan Campbell, Diana Anderson, Andreas Charidimou, Andrew Mills, Vanessa Coronel, Nacha Pierre, Beverly Reynolds, Caroline Wagner, Leanne Varga, John Roefaro, Laura Triantafylidis, Andrew E Budson
pmc-11712199.description: BackgroundLecanemab and other new amyloid‐targeting immunotherapies for Alzheimer’s disease show great promise but, may also pose significant risk for patients. To facilitate the implementation and monitoring of lecanemab infusions at our tertiary medical center, we convened an interprofessional team. The team created a number of resources including patient handouts and medical documentation templates as well as systems and processes.

pmc-12750738.title: Cranial neuropathy during severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 infection: a case report
pmc-12750738.creator: Roya Yazdani, Farzaneh Barzkar, Zahra Mirzaasgari
pmc-12750738.description: BackgroundCranial neuropathy has been reported in association with coronavirus disease 2019. Multiple reports have highlighted the possibility of Miller Fisher syndrome as a delayed immune-mediated response to severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 infection. However, cranial neuropathy during the infectious phase of coronavirus disease 2019 with positive cerebrospinal fluid polymerase chain reaction has not been reported to date.

pmc-13031494.title: Unsupervised mapping of urban tree diversity using spatially-aware visual clustering
pmc-13031494.creator: Diaa Addeen Abuhani, Marco Seccaroni, Martina Mazzarello, Imran Zualkernan, Fabio Duarte, Carlo Ratti
pmc-13031494.description: Urban tree biodiversity is critical for climate resilience, ecological stability, and livability in cities, yet most municipalities lack detailed knowledge of their canopies. Field-based inventories provide reliable estimates of Shannon and Simpson diversity but are costly and time-consuming, while supervised AI methods require labeled data that often fail to generalize across regions.

pmc-13587034.title: Market shaping for AT: scoping review and case study of an intervention
pmc-13587034.creator: Ellie Cole, Victoria Austin
pmc-13587034.description: IntroductionAssistive technology (AT) holds the potential to transform lives. With need projected to reach 3.5 billion by 2050 while access remains at only 10%, even basic AT is out-of-reach for most. Expanding access to AT is a complex systems challenge: AT markets are often small, underdeveloped and fragmented, particularly in low-income settings.

(a) Treatment of distributions and stock dispositions (1) Distributions If a United States person receives an excess distribution in respect of stock.
